goal.objective:
Implement `src/sortBy.js`, a stable multi-key sort for arrays of records. A key spec is an object `{ key, direction, nulls }`. `key` is either a function that reads the value out of a row, or a dot-separated property path such as `'user.last'` where a missing or nullish step yields `undefined`. `direction` is `'asc'` (the default) or `'desc'`. `nulls` is `'last'` (the default) or `'first'`.

Export four functions. `compareValues(a, b)` is the underlying total order over single values. `comparator(specs)` returns a comparator over rows that applies the specs in order. `sortIndices(rows, specs)` returns the permutation of indices that sorts the rows. `sortBy(rows, specs)` returns a new array of the rows in sorted order; it must not mutate its argument, and it must be stable, so rows that compare equal on every key keep their input order — in both directions, since a descending sort is not a reversed ascending sort.

Ordering is locale-free. `null`, `undefined`, and `NaN` all count as absent; absent values are equal to each other, and where they land is decided by `nulls` alone, never by `direction`, so `{ direction: 'desc', nulls: 'last' }` still puts them at the end. `compareValues` itself places absent values before every present value. Present values of the same type compare as follows: numbers numerically, with `-0` equal to `0`; strings by Unicode code point, so a code point above the basic plane sorts after `U+FFFD` and never by UTF-16 code unit, and never with `localeCompare`; booleans with `false` before `true`. When one key holds several types, order by type: numbers, then strings, then booleans. Any other type of value — an object, an array, a function, a bigint, a symbol — raises `TypeError` with message `unsupported value type: object`, naming the offending `typeof`.

Validation happens before any comparison. Rows that are not an array raise `TypeError` with message `rows must be an array`. A spec list that is not a non-empty array raises `TypeError` with message `at least one key spec is required`. A spec that is not an object raises `TypeError` with message `key spec must be an object`, and one whose key is neither a string nor a function raises `TypeError` with message `key must be a string path or a function`. An unknown direction raises `RangeError` with message `unknown direction: "up"` and an unknown null placement raises `RangeError` with message `unknown null placement: "middle"`, each quoting the offending value as JSON. Do not add dependencies; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You implement one program task in the workspace you are given, against its own test suite, and you stop when the tests pass.

The workspace is your working directory: every bash command and every file path resolves inside it, so read and edit its files by their relative paths and never search outside it.


Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: skill

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

1: import { test } from 'node:test';
2: import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
3: 
4: import { comparator, compareValues, sortBy, sortIndices } from '../src/sortBy.js';
5: 
6: /**
7:  * Deterministic 32-bit PRNG.
8:  * @param {number} seed Initial state.
9:  * @returns {() => number} Generator returning floats in [0, 1).
10:  */
11: function mulberry32(seed) {
12:   let a = seed >>> 0;
13:   return () => {
14:     a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0;
15:     let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
16:     t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
17:     return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
18:   };
19: }
20: 
21: /** Type ranks used by the independent model. */
22: const RANK = { number: 0, string: 1, boolean: 2 };
23: 
24: /**
25:  * Model test for absent values.
26:  * @param {unknown} value Value to classify.
27:  * @returns {boolean} True for null, undefined, and NaN.
28:  */
29: function absent(value) {
30:   return value === null || value === undefined || (typeof value === 'number' && Number.isNaN(value));
31: }
32: 
33: /**
34:  * Model comparison of two present values.
35:  * @param {unknown} a First value.
36:  * @param {unknown} b Second value.
37:  * @returns {number} Negative, zero, or positive.
38:  */
39: function modelCompareValues(a, b) {
40:   if (RANK[typeof a] !== RANK[typeof b]) return RANK[typeof a] - RANK[typeof b];
41:   if (typeof a === 'string') {
42:     const left = [...a].map((c) => c.codePointAt(0));
43:     const right = [...b].map((c) => c.codePointAt(0));
44:     for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(left.length, right.length); i += 1) {
45:       if (left[i] !== right[i]) return left[i] - right[i];
46:     }
47:     return left.length - right.length;
48:   }
49:   if (typeof a === 'boolean') return (a ? 1 : 0) - (b ? 1 : 0);
50:   return a === b ? 0 : a < b ? -1 : 1;
51: }
52: 
53: /**
54:  * Independent stable multi-key sort used as the model.
55:  * @param {object[]} rows Rows to order.
56:  * @param {object[]} specs Key specs.
57:  * @returns {object[]} Sorted copy.
58:  */
59: function modelSort(rows, specs) {
60:   const read = (row, key) => (typeof key === 'function' ? key(row) : key.split('.').reduce((v, p) => (v == null ? undefined : v[p]), row));
61:   const compare = (a, b) => {
62:     for (const spec of specs) {
63:       const left = read(a, spec.key);
64:       const right = read(b, spec.key);
65:       if (absent(left) || absent(right)) {
66:         if (absent(left) && absent(right)) continue;
67:         const nullsFirst = (spec.nulls ?? 'last') === 'first';
68:         return (absent(left) ? -1 : 1) * (nullsFirst ? 1 : -1);
69:       }
70:       const order = modelCompareValues(left, right);
71:       if (order !== 0) return order * ((spec.direction ?? 'asc') === 'asc' ? 1 : -1);
72:     }
73:     return 0;
74:   };
75:   const items = rows.map((row, index) => ({ row, index }));
76:   for (let i = 1; i < items.length; i += 1) {
77:     const item = items[i];
78:     let j = i - 1;
79:     while (j >= 0 && compare(items[j].row, item.row) > 0) {
80:       items[j + 1] = items[j];
81:       j -= 1;
82:     }
83:     items[j + 1] = item;
84:   }
85:   return items.map((item) => item.row);
86: }
87: 
88: test('compareValues orders absent values first, then by type rank', () => {
89:   assert.equal(compareValues(null, 3), -1);
90:   assert.equal(compareValues(3, undefined), 1);
91:   assert.equal(compareValues(null, undefined), 0);
92:   assert.equal(compareValues(Number.NaN, null), 0);
93:   assert.equal(compareValues(Number.NaN, -5), -1);
94:   assert.equal(compareValues(9, 'a'), -1);
95:   assert.equal(compareValues('a', false), -1);
96: });
97: 
98: test('compareValues is locale-free and compares strings by code point', () => {
99:   assert.ok(compareValues('A', 'a') < 0);
100:   assert.ok(compareValues('apple', 'Apple') > 0);
101:   assert.ok(compareValues('ab', 'abc') < 0);
102:   assert.ok(compareValues('', 'a') < 0);
103:   assert.ok(compareValues('\u{1F600}', '\uFFFD') > 0);
104:   assert.ok(compareValues('\uFF10', '\u{1F600}') < 0);
105:   assert.equal(compareValues('e\u0301', 'e\u0301'), 0);
106:   assert.ok(compareValues('e\u0301', '\u00E9') < 0);
107: });
108: 
109: test('compareValues handles numeric and boolean edges', () => {
110:   assert.equal(compareValues(-0, 0), 0);
111:   assert.equal(compareValues(0, 1e-9), -1);
112:   assert.equal(compareValues(Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY, -1e308), -1);
113:   assert.equal(compareValues(false, true), -1);
114:   assert.throws(() => compareValues({}, 1), { name: 'TypeError', message: 'unsupported value type: object' });
115:   assert.throws(() => compareValues(1, () => 1), { name: 'TypeError', message: 'unsupported value type: function' });
116:   assert.throws(() => compareValues(1n, 2), { name: 'TypeError', message: 'unsupported value type: bigint' });
117: });
118: 
119: test('sortBy orders by one key and leaves the input untouched', () => {
120:   const rows = [{ n: 3 }, { n: 1 }, { n: 2 }];
121:   const sorted = sortBy(rows, [{ key: 'n' }]);
122:   assert.deepEqual(sorted.map((r) => r.n), [1, 2, 3]);
123:   assert.deepEqual(rows.map((r) => r.n), [3, 1, 2]);
124:   assert.notEqual(sorted, rows);
125:   assert.equal(sorted[0], rows[1]);
126:   assert.deepEqual(sortBy(rows, [{ key: 'n', direction: 'desc' }]).map((r) => r.n), [3, 2, 1]);
127:   assert.deepEqual(sortBy([], [{ key: 'n' }]), []);
128: });
129: 
130: test('sortBy is stable in both directions', () => {
131:   const rows = [
132:     { g: 'x', id: 0 }, { g: 'y', id: 1 }, { g: 'x', id: 2 },
133:     { g: 'y', id: 3 }, { g: 'x', id: 4 }, { g: 'y', id: 5 },
134:   ];
135:   assert.deepEqual(sortBy(rows, [{ key: 'g' }]).map((r) => r.id), [0, 2, 4, 1, 3, 5]);
136:   assert.deepEqual(sortBy(rows, [{ key: 'g', direction: 'desc' }]).map((r) => r.id), [1, 3, 5, 0, 2, 4]);
137:   const flat = Array.from({ length: 40 }, (_, id) => ({ g: 0, id }));
138:   assert.deepEqual(sortBy(flat, [{ key: 'g', direction: 'desc' }]).map((r) => r.id), flat.map((r) => r.id));
139:   assert.deepEqual(sortIndices(flat, [{ key: 'g' }]), flat.map((_, i) => i));

142: test('null placement is independent of direction', () => {
143:   const rows = [{ v: 2 }, { v: null }, { v: 1 }, { v: undefined }, { v: Number.NaN }];
144:   const label = (list) => list.map((r) => (typeof r.v === 'number' && !Number.isNaN(r.v) ? r.v : 'nil'));
145:   assert.deepEqual(label(sortBy(rows, [{ key: 'v' }])), [1, 2, 'nil', 'nil', 'nil']);
146:   assert.deepEqual(label(sortBy(rows, [{ key: 'v', nulls: 'first' }])), ['nil', 'nil', 'nil', 1, 2]);
147:   assert.deepEqual(label(sortBy(rows, [{ key: 'v', direction: 'desc' }])), [2, 1, 'nil', 'nil', 'nil']);
148:   assert.deepEqual(label(sortBy(rows, [{ key: 'v', direction: 'desc', nulls: 'first' }])), ['nil', 'nil', 'nil', 2, 1]);
149:   assert.deepEqual(sortBy(rows, [{ key: 'v', nulls: 'first' }]).slice(0, 3).map((r) => rows.indexOf(r)), [1, 3, 4]);

152: test('multiple keys apply in order with per-key direction and paths', () => {
153:   const rows = [
154:     { user: { last: 'Ng', first: 'Bo' }, score: 5 },
155:     { user: { last: 'ng', first: 'Al' }, score: 9 },
156:     { user: { last: 'Ng', first: 'Al' }, score: 7 },
157:     { user: { last: 'Ng' }, score: 9 },

159:   const out = sortBy(rows, [{ key: 'user.last' }, { key: 'user.first', nulls: 'first' }]);
160:   assert.deepEqual(out.map((r) => r.score), [9, 7, 5, 9]);
161:   const byScore = sortBy(rows, [{ key: 'score', direction: 'desc' }, { key: 'user.first' }]);
162:   assert.deepEqual(byScore.map((r) => r.user.first), ['Al', undefined, 'Al', 'Bo']);
163:   const byLength = sortBy(rows, [{ key: (row) => row.user.last.length }, { key: 'score', direction: 'desc' }]);
164:   assert.deepEqual(byLength.map((r) => r.score), [9, 9, 7, 5]);
165:   assert.deepEqual(sortBy(rows, [{ key: 'missing.deep.path' }]).map((r) => r.score), [5, 9, 7, 9]);
166: });

169:   const rows = [{ a: 2, b: 'x' }, { a: 1, b: 'y' }, { a: 2, b: 'a' }];
170:   const specs = [{ key: 'a' }, { key: 'b', direction: 'desc' }];
171:   const compare = comparator(specs);
172:   assert.equal(compare(rows[0], rows[1]) > 0, true);
173:   assert.equal(compare(rows[0], rows[2]) < 0, true);
174:   assert.equal(compare(rows[0], rows[0]), 0);
175:   assert.deepEqual(sortIndices(rows, specs), [1, 0, 2]);

177: });

goal.objective:
Implement `src/sortBy.js`, a stable multi-key sort for arrays of records. A key spec is an object `{ key, direction, nulls }`. `key` is either a function that reads the value out of a row, or a dot-separated property path such as `'user.last'` where a missing or nullish step yields `undefined`. `direction` is `'asc'` (the default) or `'desc'`. `nulls` is `'last'` (the default) or `'first'`.

Export four functions. `compareValues(a, b)` is the underlying total order over single values. `comparator(specs)` returns a comparator over rows that applies the specs in order. `sortIndices(rows, specs)` returns the permutation of indices that sorts the rows. `sortBy(rows, specs)` returns a new array of the rows in sorted order; it must not mutate its argument, and it must be stable, so rows that compare equal on every key keep their input order — in both directions, since a descending sort is not a reversed ascending sort.

Ordering is locale-free. `null`, `undefined`, and `NaN` all count as absent; absent values are equal to each other, and where they land is decided by `nulls` alone, never by `direction`, so `{ direction: 'desc', nulls: 'last' }` still puts them at the end. `compareValues` itself places absent values before every present value. Present values of the same type compare as follows: numbers numerically, with `-0` equal to `0`; strings by Unicode code point, so a code point above the basic plane sorts after `U+FFFD` and never by UTF-16 code unit, and never with `localeCompare`; booleans with `false` before `true`. When one key holds several types, order by type: numbers, then strings, then booleans. Any other type of value — an object, an array, a function, a bigint, a symbol — raises `TypeError` with message `unsupported value type: object`, naming the offending `typeof`.

Validation happens before any comparison. Rows that are not an array raise `TypeError` with message `rows must be an array`. A spec list that is not a non-empty array raises `TypeError` with message `at least one key spec is required`. A spec that is not an object raises `TypeError` with message `key spec must be an object`, and one whose key is neither a string nor a function raises `TypeError` with message `key must be a string path or a function`. An unknown direction raises `RangeError` with message `unknown direction: "up"` and an unknown null placement raises `RangeError` with message `unknown null placement: "middle"`, each quoting the offending value as JSON. Do not add dependencies; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.
